learningObjective: State the semantics of a CUDA stream (an in-order queue of device work) and a CUDA event (a synchronization point recordable on a stream), and their role in a runtime.

canonicalClaims.claim: A CUDA stream is a logical in-order queue: within a stream, operations execute in issue order; across streams, operations may execute concurrently. Events are synchronization markers recorded on a stream that other streams or the host can wait on.
conditions: Sufficient device resources to permit inter-stream concurrency when data dependencies permit.
nonImplications: Does not imply that cross-stream operations always run concurrently; they may serialize when resource-limited.
Does not imply events are the only synchronization mechanism; stream-level and device-level synchronize APIs exist.

misconceptions.claim: A stream is bound to a specific SM group.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Streams are logical queues; the scheduler assigns work to SMs dynamically.
Events are synchronization primitives; performance counters live in Nsight Compute's metrics.
Streams do not contain data; they are execution queues.
Within-stream ordering is guaranteed by the API contract.
